content.title: Is McDonald's Open or Closed on Easter Sunday?
content.text: Key PointsEaster spending expected to hit a record $24.9 billion, NRF survey reports.Most McDonald’s locations are open on Easter, but hours vary by location.McDonald’s began in 1954 and now operates over 36,000 restaurants worldwide. Easter Sunday is finally here and consumers are expected to spend a record amount on the popular holiday. “Consumer spending on Easter is expected to reach a record total of $24.9 billion this year, according to the annual survey released today by the National Retail Federation and Prosper Insights & Analytics,” the NRF announced. The amount surpasses the previous record of $24 billion set in 2023. On a per-person basis, shoppers are budgeting a record high of $195.59, up from the previous record of $192.01 in 2023. “While economic uncertainty remains on the minds of many, consumers are still focused on holiday celebrations like Easter,” NRF Chief Economist and Executive Director of Research Mark Mathews said. “Holidays provide an important opportunity for families to reconnect and create lasting memories, even as economic conditions fluctuate.” While record spending is in the forecast, some might still be looking for less expensive options for meals around the holiday with many turning to fast food restaurants like McDonald’s. The short answer is yes. Most McDonald’s locations in the United States are open on holidays, but the hours will vary by locations, a spokesperson told Today. The fast food restaurant chain recommends using the store location to confirm hours at local stores. To find a McDonald’s near you or check hours, see the store locator right here. When Was McDonald’s Founded? Back in 1954, a man named Ray Kroc discovered a small burger restaurant in California and wrote the first page of McDonald’s history, the McDonald’s website says. “From humble beginnings as a small restaurant, we’re proud to have become one of the world’s leading restaurant chains with more than 36,000 restaurants in more than 100 countries,” the restaurant proudly claimed.
